'''Anke Weidenkaff''' (December 27, 1966 in [[Hanover]], Germany) is a German-Swiss chemist and materials scientist. Since 2018, she has been head of the Materials & Resources Group at the Faculty of Materials Science at [[Technische Universität Darmstadt|Technical University Darmstadt]].

== Biography ==
Weidenkaff was born in Hanover, Germany, and studied chemistry at the [[University of Hamburg]]. She received her PhD in 2000 from [[ETH Zurich]] in the Department of Chemistry. In 2006, she received the Venia Legendi for Solid State Chemistry and Materials Science from the [[University of Augsburg]] and became section head at the [[Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology|Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology (Empa)]] and associated professor at the [[University of Bern]]. From 2013 to 2018, she was director of the Institute of Materials Science at the [[University of Stuttgart]], where she chaired the Department of Chemical Materials Synthesis.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Fraunhofer IWKS - About us |url=https://www.iwks.fraunhofer.de/en/about-us/head-of-Fraunhofer-IWKS.html |access-date=2022-01-13}}</ref> Weidenkaff was director of Fraunhofer Research Institution for Materials Recycling and Resource Strategies, a research institute of the [[Fraunhofer Society]], from 2018 until 2024.<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2019-03-26 |title=OB begrüßt Fraunhofer Projektgruppenleiterin Prof. Dr. Weidenkaff |trans-title=Lord Mayor welcomes Fraunhofer project group leader Prof. Dr. Weidenkaff |url=http://www.presse-service.de/data.aspx/static/1011892F.html |language=German |location=Hanau, Germany |publisher=Stadt Hanau |access-date=2022-03-12}}</ref> Weidenkaff is professor at [[Technical University Darmstadt]] in the field of material science and resource management.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mawi.tu-darmstadt.de/mr/mr/index~1.en.jsp |title=Materials and Resources Group | website=Technical University of Darmstadt |access-date=2024-03-10}}</ref>

From 2016 to 2019, she was president of the [[European Thermoelectric Society|European Thermoelectric Society (ETS)]], of which she had been a board member since 2007.<ref name=":0" /> She is an elected member of the European Materials Research Society's (E-MRS) Executive Committee <ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.european-mrs.com/about/scientific-council |title=E-MRS Scientific Council | website=European Materials Research Society |access-date=2024-03-10}}</ref> and was chair of the 2019 E-MRS Spring Meeting.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.european-mrs.com/meetings/2019-spring-meeting |title=2019 Spring Meeting - EMRS |website=European Materials Research Society (E-MRS) |access-date=2024-04-20}}</ref> Weidenkaff was a member of the [[German Advisory Council on Global Change|German Advisory Council on Global Change (WBGU)]]<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2020-10-14 |title=Bundeskabinett beruft WBGU-Mitglieder |trans-title=Federal Cabinet appoints WBGU members |url=https://www.bmuv.de/pressemitteilung/bundeskabinett-beruft-wbgu-mitglieder |language=German |location=Berlin, Germany |publisher=German Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation, Nuclear Safety and Consumer Protection |access-date=2022-03-12}}</ref> from 2020 to 2024. She was elected as a member to the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] and the [[Acatech|German Academy of Science and Engineering]] in 2023.

== Research ==
Weidenkaff's main areas of research and expertise<ref>{{Cite web|title=Publications of Anke Weidenkaff on Google Scholar|url=https://scholar.google.de/citations?hl=de&user=QDCB9qkAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&sortby=pubdate|access-date=2022-03-12}}</ref> are materials science and resource strategies,<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2021-12-22 |title=Rohstoffversorgung langfristig sichern |trans-title=Securing raw material supplies in the long term |url=https://www.vbw-bayern.de/vbw/Themen-und-Services/Rohstoffe-Ressourcen/R%C3%BCckblick-Rohstoffversorgung-langfristig-sichern.jsp |language=German |location=Munich, Germany |publisher=vbw – Vereinigung der Bayerischen Wirtschaft e. V. |access-date=2022-03-12}}</ref> including the development, synthesis chemistry, and characterization of substitute materials for energy conversion and storage. Building on scientific knowledge of solid-state chemistry, her current work focuses on materials science and specifically the development of regenerative, sustainable materials and next-generation process technologies for fast and efficiently closed materials cycles. Anke Weidenkaff and her team are currently working on technologies for the production of (green) [[hydrogen]] including photoelectrochemical [[water splitting]],<ref name="DF">{{cite press release |first=Arndt |last=Reuning |date=2016-02-29 |title=Perowskit-Technologie - Ungewöhnliches Material für Solarzellen |trans-title=Perovskite technology - Unusual material for solar cells |url=https://www.deutschlandfunk.de/perowskit-technologie-ungewoehnliches-material-fuer-100.html |language=German |location=Cologne, Germany |publisher=Deutschalndfunk |access-date=2022-03-12}}</ref> the production of [[carbon nanotube]]s using microwave plasma synthesis for carbon storage, and sustainable [[perovskite]] materials.<ref name="DF" /> She is also involved in the development of [[thermoelectrics]], electroceramics and ceramic membranes. She conducts research on sustainable materials and recycling technologies for [[Battery recycling|batteries]] and [[fuel cell]]s. Another focus of her work is "Green ICT", the development of sustainable materials and processes for information and communication technology.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.iwks.fraunhofer.de/en/projects/current-projects/green2-ICT.html |title=Attract Group 'green²ICT' | website=Fraunhofer Research Institution for Materials Recycling and Resource Strategies (IWKS) |access-date=2024-04-20}}</ref>

== International recognition and activities ==

* 2008: Visiting professor, [[Case Western Reserve University|Case Western Reserve University (CWRU)]] and visiting scientist [[Glenn Research Center|NASA Glenn Research Centre]], Cleveland, USA{{Relevance inline|date=March 2024}}
* 2011: [[Kavli Foundation (United States)|Kavli Foundation]] Lectureship prize{{Relevance inline|date=March 2024}}
* 2012 - 2013: Editor in Chief and Member of the Editorial Board of “Energy Quarterly”; Member of the Advisory Board of the MRS Book Series on Energy and Sustainability
* 2015 - 2017: Member of the Board of Directors, [[Materials Research Society|Materials Research Society (MRS)]]
* 2016 - 2019: President of the [[European Thermoelectric Society|European Thermoelectric Society (ETS)]]
* 2020 - 2024: Member of the [[German Advisory Council on Global Change|German Advisory Council on Global Change (WBGU)]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Anke Weidenkaff |url=https://www.wbgu.de/en/the-wbgu/current-members-of-the-council/prof-dr-anke-weidenkaff |access-date=2024-01-08 |website=www.wbgu.de}}</ref>
* 2022: [[Karl Wolfgang Boer|Karl W. Böer]] Renewable Energy Mid-Career Award<ref>{{cite press release |first=Beth |last=Miller |date=2022-04-06 |title=Winners of 2022 Böer awards announced |url=https://www.udel.edu/udaily/2022/april/karl-boer-medal-photovoltaics-sustainable-energy-vasilis-fthenakis-anke-weidenkaff/ |language=English |location=Newark, United States of America |publisher=University of Delaware |access-date=2022-08-20}}</ref>
* since 2023: Member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Member: Anke Weidenkaff |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/anke-weidenkaff/ |access-date=2024-01-08 |website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina |language=en-US}}</ref>
* since 2023: Member of the [[Acatech]], the German National Academy of Science and Engineering.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-12-06 |title=39 leading scientists join the ranks of acatech |url=https://en.acatech.de/allgemein/39-leading-scientists-join-the-ranks-of-acatech/ |access-date=2024-01-08 |website=acatech - National Academy of Science and Engineering |language=en-GB}}</ref>
